speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for seeing me. You mentioned increasing pain and swelling in your left knee for two months; to help narrow this down, does the pain worsen with activity or is it present even at rest?

Also, have you noticed any redness, warmth, or a history of fever associated with this joint?

Finally, have you experienced any recent trauma, or do you have a history of gout or rheumatoid arthritis?

speaker: Patient
text: 24-year-old male. The patient reports increasing pain and swelling of the left knee over 2 months. Describes the pain as severe enough to awaken him from sleep on several occasions. States he tried taking ibuprofen with no relief. No family or personal history of significant illnesses.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Idiopathic Juvenile Arthritis (Oligoarticular)

Based on your severe pain awakening you from sleep and lack of response to NSAIDs, this suggests an inflammatory rather than mechanical cause. Given your age of 24 and the absence of trauma or prior arthritis history, we must rule out other inflammatory conditions. Have you noticed any morning stiffness lasting more than 30 minutes?
